description: Locates the fit that produced the published kappa. It survives under computations/_deprecated/. The published value is the 3He arm alone; the T arm has the opposite sign; and the producing witness records hypothesis_supported=false. The fit was to Delta_coupling, not to binding energy as the content block states.

original_verdict.interpretation: The interface-excess hypothesis predicts a single constant κ (in units of h · E_0) across all atoms. If ³He and T give the same κ to ≤ 5% AND ⁴He has residual ≤ 5% of base, the hypothesis is supported. The pp interface (σ) and nn interface (σ⁻¹) contribute opposite-sign u-pole corrections; doubly-magic atoms have balanced (pp = nn) counts and the corrections cancel.

data.finding: The conjecture's 0.034% agreement is with one arm of a two-arm measurement whose own probe recorded the single-kappa hypothesis as unsupported. The block reports the value as observed 'at the single-magic anchors' (plural); the anchors disagree in sign.

assertions.name: published_kappa_is_the_3He_arm_alone
assertions.detail: the value the content block carries is exactly the 3He anchor's slope, to the last bit -- not a combination of the two single-magic anchors

assertions.name: the_two_single_magic_anchors_disagree_in_sign
assertions.detail: 3He gives -1.070791 MeV, T gives +0.202309 MeV -- opposite signs, ratio 5.3x

assertions.name: the_producing_probe_recorded_its_hypothesis_as_unsupported
assertions.detail: the witness carries hypothesis_supported=false and slope_consistent_to_5pct=false -- the fit refuted itself at the time

assertions.name: the_fit_was_to_delta_coupling_not_to_binding
assertions.detail: the probe's hypothesis is about Delta_coupling; the content block describes kappa as an atomic-BINDING coefficient -- different observables

assertions.name: composition_sweep_uses_convention_C1
assertions.detail: n_pp = max(0, Z-1) and n_nn = max(0, N-1) hold on every swept row -- the same convention selected on corpus-structure grounds elsewhere
